key_insight: This synthesis links stochastic transport models with rigorous analysis, data-driven calibration and high-dimensional Bayesian inference for uncertainty-aware geophysical forecasting.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports uncertainty quantification and data assimilation in geophysical fluid simulations, with potential value for ocean forecasting.
method: Establish well-posedness, regularity and approximation theory for stochastic transport equations.
Calibrate transport uncertainty using observations, high-resolution simulations, reduced-order models and generative approaches.
Apply particle filtering and machine-learning uncertainty quantification to Bayesian data assimilation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reviews theory and calibration using observational and simulation data, but reports no quantitative benchmarks or forecasting gains.
watch_item: Scalability and calibration reliability in high-dimensional operational models require validation beyond the abstract's synthesis.
paper_title: From Stochastic Transport Models to High-Dimensional Bayesian Inference
